draft.title: The hypotenuse and Pythagoras' theorem
card: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is the side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.
Pythagoras' theorem links the three sides. The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.
If the hypotenuse is \(c\) and the other sides are \(a\) and \(b\), then \(c^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}\).
A triangle has shorter sides 3 and 4, and hypotenuse 5. Check: \(3^{2} + 4^{2} = 9 + 16 = 25\), and \(5^{2} = 25\).
draft.remember: The hypotenuse faces the right angle, and its square equals the sum of the other two squares.

a.q: A triangle has a right angle at corner B. Which side lies directly across from corner B, and so is the hypotenuse?
opts: The side joining the other two corners
A side that touches corner B
The shortest side of the triangle
The side drawn along the bottom
a.why: The hypotenuse is opposite the right angle, so it joins the two corners that are not the right angle. The sides touching corner B are the two shorter sides. Which side sits at the bottom depends only on how the triangle is turned.
a.clue: Find the right angle, then look across the triangle.

b.q: A right-angled triangle has sides 5, 12 and 13. Which equation is correct for it?
b.why: The hypotenuse is the longest side, 13, so its square is on its own: \(169 = 25 + 144\). The last option adds the sides without squaring them, and \(5 + 12 = 17\), not 13.
b.clue: Put the longest side on its own, and square every side.
